A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LapEigvals research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, including the rotated tables, and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original hallucination-detection experiments on six datasets and three LLMs, statistical feature analyses, and ablations (Table 1, Section 6, and appendices).

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds results for GSM8K, two Mistral models, hidden-state probes, judge agreement, training-data requirements, and feature perturbations.

M1.justification: Both versions use normalized attention-derived Laplacians, their largest diagonal eigenvalues across heads and layers, PCA, and logistic regression. Equation (2) rewrites the causal degree normalization using T-i; the surrounding description retains the same procedure. New proofs and implementation disclosures do not establish a different algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds the GSM8K test set of 1,319 mathematics problems to the six retained QA datasets. This extends evaluation to mathematical reasoning and adds transfers between mathematics and the existing QA domains (Section 4.1 and Table 11).

E2.justification: v1 evaluates attention-derived comparators only. v2 adds a hidden-state comparator family: PCA-projected logistic-regression probes using the last answer token, with both per-layer and all-layer variants (Appendix G.4, Table 10). AttentionScore, AttnLogDet, and AttnEigvals remain.

E3.justification: v2 expands from three to five evaluated LLMs by adding Mistral-Nemo and Mistral-Small-24B at both decoding temperatures. Added protocols include GSM8K exact-match labeling with a dedicated reasoning prompt, precision/recall at threshold 0.5, stratified training fractions, and controlled feature-noise settings. The existing 80/20 stratified split and principal probe settings are retained.

E4.justification: New analyses test agreement between gpt-4o-mini and gpt-4.1 labels, performance with reduced training data, and sensitivity to Gaussian perturbations before eigenvalue sorting (Appendices F, J, K). Precision/recall analysis is also added, and existing eigenvalue-count, layer, and transfer studies are extended to the added configurations.

E5.justification: Appendix K and Table 13 newly report means and standard deviations across five perturbation runs. Both versions retain single-run reporting for Table 1 and standard deviations over ten balanced samples in the temperature study. This is a localized expansion of uncertainty reporting, not an increase in repetitions for the main benchmarks.

E6.justification: Original Table 1 scores and shared extended-comparison results are retained, while substantial new benchmark and diagnostic results appear. For example, v2 reports GSM8K AUROC 0.872 for Llama-3.1-8B LapEigvals versus 0.838 for AttnEigvals, and Table 13 shows deterioration under large perturbations. Some newly reported values conflict internally: Llama-3.2-3B LapEigvals on NQOpen at temperature 1.0 is 0.798 in Table 10 but 0.693 in Table 1; this cannot establish a performance improvement.

T1.justification: v2 corrects the above-diagonal attention constraint from 1 to 0 and adds elementary proofs that Laplacian eigenvalues lie in [-1,1] and include a zero eigenvalue (Appendix B). Appendix L adds an operation-count argument for quadratic degree computation and eigenvalue sorting. These are limited formal additions to the retained mathematical framework.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: Laplacian spectral features indicate hallucinations, LapEigvals achieves leading attention-based detection performance, and ablations support robustness and generalization. Expanded experiments provide additional support without redefining those contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of GSM8K transfer failures as domain mismatch, judge agreement as a label-quality proxy, bfloat16 rounding as a stabilizing mechanism, and precision/recall tradeoffs. It also discusses attention-materialization and FlashAttention constraints. Some additions are overstated: Appendix G.4 claims consistent superiority over all-layer hidden-state probes despite Table 10 exceptions, and Appendix F attributes low agreement to TriviaQA although Table 4 shows the lowest agreement for TruthfulQA.

D1.justification: v2 documents bfloat16 storage, feature computation fused with inference, H100 hardware for the 24B model, hidden-state feature construction, a GSM8K prompt, expanded optimal hyperparameters, and labeling-cost estimates. It updates the stated repository destination from lapeig to lapeigvals and replaces the uncertain TriviaQA licensing statement with Apache 2.0. The earlier implementation section is relocated to Appendix C.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for GSM8K, the two Mistral models, Wu et al., Mann–Whitney, and FlashAttention. It more explicitly distinguishes LapEigvals from AttentionScore through full-attention information and all-layer features. The broader related-work organization and research positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: The main section order and most prose are retained. v2 revises motivation, method, and baseline explanations, standardizes spelling, corrects several names and cross-references, and relocates implementation details. Appendix organization expands, but the retained narrative is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: Main Figures 4–5 now display Mistral-Small-24B, while the original multi-model analyses are retained and expanded in appendix Figures 10–11. Dataset plots and benchmark tables expand, new diagnostic tables appear, and the original extended comparison is split into Tables 6–7. Heatmaps and diagrams are also redrawn, producing substantial display and layout changes.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important validation gaps in v1 through hidden-state controls, mathematics evaluated by exact match, larger model configurations, judge-agreement checks, and training-size and perturbation analyses. These additions substantially improve assessment of the method's usefulness and failure boundaries while preserving the original evidence. Conflicting Table 10 values and overstated interpretations weaken parts of the revision, but do not outweigh the broader validation and practical documentation.
